title: Full aid details, smarter search, faster dams
changes: Fixed: on phones, holding a finger on the map opened the menu but iOS also offered to copy or save the map image; now only the LightKeeper menu appears.
On phones the long-press menu opens as a centered card with an X to close; every option fits and the list scrolls if needed.
Fixed: on iPhone home-screen mode the search bar and district picker sat under the clock and battery; the top bar now starts below them.
New "LightKeeper V1" dropdown on the Version page and in What's new: every update to the original app, October 2025 to April 2026.
Fixed: the Version and Data & notices pages would not open on iPhone (Safari said the response "has redirections").
Adding the site to your home screen now shows a lighthouse icon instead of a plain letter.
New Dams button next to Boat Ramps, Hotels and Parks: dam markers show on the map whenever you zoom in (they used to appear only from the right-click menu).

Aid cards list the light's characteristic, color, range (visibility), focal plane and structure height under Identity. Range and structure height were blank for every aid before; they are now read from the Light List.
Search finds aids from any part of the name in any order: "goose 4", "lit goo res 12" and "lt 2" all work, as do Light List numbers.
Search shows lights first, then daybeacons and buoys, with numbers in order (Light 2 before Light 10) and up to 20 aids in a scrolling list.
Light List numbers show cleanly (13672.3 instead of 13672.300000000001).
Dams no longer disappear when zoomed out, and 875 dam cards fill in Army Corps releases and water levels in about 1 to 2 seconds.
Water temperature now comes from the nearest river gauge in well under a second at most spots (Fashion Reef: 4 mi away instead of Tacoma, 117 mi).
Satellite view on the website shows road and place names again.
The website has a Version page with the latest updates and fixes, known issues and the to-do list, and it always loads the newest version after an update.

One search box at the top finds aids by name or Light List number anywhere in the picked district, plus ramps and hotels; aid results show instantly.

Picking a district downloads just that district's places, with a size and time estimate.

title: Fixes and improvements
changes: Lodging and parks no longer disappear when the public OpenStreetMap servers are busy: the app now checks Photon and Nominatim as well and shows whatever answers first.
Aid cards show the nearest boat ramp; click it to draw the route to the ramp. Where water geometry is not available yet the line is dashed and marked as a straight line.
Aid cards show the Coast Guard district and sector as links that open the unit's contact card.
Tides, currents and river gages open with a chart plus the table.
The "Tides here" and similar lookups search progressively farther and say how far away the station is instead of failing at 40 miles.
Water temperature now returns the nearest reading with its distance instead of "no station nearby".

Google Places key can be entered in Settings so every place is verified against Google (optional).
Report-a-bug button says "Aye aye" and the What's new entry is dated October 20.

title: LightKeeper 2 — a fresh start
summary: LightKeeper was rebuilt from the ground up with a simpler layout, a native window instead of a browser tab, and much faster downloads.
changes: Opens in its own window — no browser needed.
One sidebar with six sections: Aids, Trip, Measure, Water, Weather and Settings. One detail card for everything you click.

The whole USCG Light List (all nine districts, about 54,000 aids) downloads in under a minute on first launch, and every later launch checks for changes in seconds and tells you what moved, changed or was added or removed.
Boat ramps, hotels and parks are properly named. Click one to see its address, phone number and website when they exist.
Right-click anywhere on the map for tides, currents, river gages, dam releases, weather, water temperature, nearby ramps and lodging, or to start measuring.
Hover the map for a subtle hint; turn on 'nearest stations' in the Water panel to see the closest tide, gage and dam stations as you move.
Trip planner: tick aids, set days, speed and hours, and get a day-by-day plan with launch and recovery ramps, lodging, weather, tides and a PDF export.
Measure tool with distance in NM, miles or km and true course per leg. Drag points to move them, right-click to remove.
Water panel: NOAA tide and current predictions, USGS river gages (level, flow, temperature), USACE dam pool, inflow and outflow.
Backup sources: if the National Weather Service or NOAA tides are down, forecasts and tides come from Open-Meteo so you still get data.
Tides, currents and river gages open with a chart (highs and lows, flood and ebb, 7-day level) plus the table.

Works offline: the Light List, places, station lists and every map tile you have viewed are cached in your AppData folder. After first launch the app also pre-caches the US base map, satellite imagery around every aid, and ramps and lodging per district in the background.
NOAA ENC chart overlay (Charts button) with caching.
District picker filters the map to one district or shows all.
Zoom all the way to street level on every base map.
Settings: vessel speed and fuel, offline map downloads, backup export/import of your settings and saved trips, optional Mapbox key.
Fixed: secure connections to map and chart services on PCs whose Windows certificate store is out of date.
Report a bug button (Teams or email) and a What's new tab in the rail.
